(By Smt. Girija S. Hiremath, Hcgp For R1, R2, R3 & R7;
 Sri Bhushan B. Kulkarni, Advocate For R4-R6)
 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227
Of The Constitution Of India, Praying To Issue Writ Or
Order Or Direction, In The Nature Of Mandamus Directing
The Respondents For Considering The Representations
Produced At Annexure-D To D4 Dated 19.01.2022 And
Initiate Acquisition Proceedings To The Land Of The
Petitioner Bearing Sy.No.62/1 Measuring 04 A-07 G Of
Aadagal Village, Tq: Badami And Dist: Bagalkot, With All
Statutory Benefits And Etc.
 This Petition Coming On For Orders This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order
1.

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, learned HCGP for the respondent Nos.1, 2, 3 and 7,
and Sri Bhushan B.Kulkarni, learned counsel for the respondent Nos.4 to 6.
2

This petition is filed by the petitioner seeking a writ of mandamus seeking direction to the respondents to consider the representation dated 19.01.2022 and initiate acquisition proceedings with respect to the land of the petitioner bearing Survey No.62/1, measuring 4 acres 7 NC:
2024:KHC-D:9513 guntas in Adagal village, taluk Badami, district Bagalkot with all statutory benefits.
Martengyavva W/O Hanamappa ... vs The State on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68599389/
2 3.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that, he is the owner of the agricultural land in Survey No.62/1, measuring 4 acres 7 guntas of Adagal village, taluk Badami,
district Bagalkot.

She further contends that, respondent No.7 has made use of the land of the petitioner for constructing a link road from Adagal - Pattadakal by dissecting Badami - Bagalkot main road at Adagal village.
The construction formation of the road was carried through the lands of the petitioner without initiating acquisition proceedings.

She further contends that, it is the joint responsibility of respondent Nos.4, 5, 6 and 7, pursuant to the coming into force of Panchayat Raj Act, to tender just and fair compensation amount for having utilized the land of the petitioner.
4. The petitioner on several occasions made request in writing and given representation to the respondents to initiate acquisition proceedings and pass NC: 2024:KHC-D:9513 suitable orders.
Nothing was considered.
Hence, representation on 19.01.2022 came to be made which also did not yield any result.

Hence, she is before this Court seeking a writ of mandamus as against the respondents to initiate suitable acquisition proceedings for having utilized the land of the petitioner and pay the compensation in accordance with law.
and learned counsel for the respondent Nos.4 to 6 have filed their respective statement of objections.

6. Per contra, learned HCGP contends and has taken a plea in the statement at paragraph No.2 that the land of the petitioners at Survey No.62/1 of Adagal village of Badami taluk, Bagalkot district is not at all encroached by the State and no road is formed in the aforesaid petitioner's land.

It is also stated and contended by the learned HCGP that, the petitioner's land in Survey No.62/1, measuring 4 acres 7 guntas does not come within the road formed, and it excludes the existing road.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:9513

So also, learned counsel for the respondent Nos.4 to 6 contends that, the road so formed by the State is not maintained by the respondent Nos.4 to 6 and they are not one who have constructed or maintaining the road as it is the State which is maintaining the road.
He also subscribes to the arguments put forth by the learned HCGP.

7. In view of the statement of objections and the contentions taken by the learned HCGP and respondent Nos.4 to 6 that the land of the petitioner in Survey No.62/1, measuring 4 acres 7 guntas having not been utilized for the acquisition, the question of considering the representation would not arise as the reply herein is as good as the answer/reply to the representation made by the petitioner.
This Court cannot go into the disputed questions of fact as to whether the land is acquired or not.
It is for the petitioner to ascertain on the ground reality whether the land is utilized to seek necessary acquisition proceedings in accordance with law.
In view of the above, I do not find any cogent reason to accept the petition for considering the representation as the statement made herein would be as good as answer to the representation/reply.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
Martengyavva W/O Hanamappa ... vs The State on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68599389/
3 ORDER (i) The petition is disposed of, taking into consideration the statement made by the State that the land of the petitioner in guntas is not acquired or utilized by the State or by the respondent Nos.4 to 6;
(ii) The petitioner is at liberty to initiate appropriate proceedings in the manner known to law;
Sd/-
JUDGE SVH CT:BCK Martengyavva W/O Hanamappa ... vs The State on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68599389/
